directions.name: Antioxidant
directions.description: Peptides screened for free-radical scavenging for wound dressings, tissue engineering and antioxidant coatings. Ranked by AnOxPePred's FRS head.

directions.name: Antibacterial
directions.description: Peptides screened for antibacterial activity for anti-infection dressings and medical device coatings. Ranked by iMFP-LG's AMP channel, cross-checked against AMPlify-ESM.

directions.name: Anti-inflammatory
directions.description: Peptides screened for anti-inflammatory activity for chronic wound management. The AIP models behind this direction separate functional-looking peptides from random fragments rather than measuring anti-inflammatory activity, so the score is a ranking signal and is never presented as a probability.

directions.name: Anti-melanin Deposition
directions.description: Peptides screened for tyrosinase inhibition for skin-brightening functional materials. Ranked by TIPred.

routes.name: Wound Dressing
routes.contact_interface: Applied to an open wound, contacting the wound bed and tissue fluid directly
routes.immune_exposure: High — the skin barrier is already broken, so the construct contacts tissue fluid directly

screening.threshold_note: The barrier is breached and the construct contacts tissue fluid directly, so immune exposure is in the same band as injection. The gate is tightened to 0.35 rather than treated as intact skin.

application_techniques: Direct application to the wound bed

routes.name: Mask / Patch
routes.contact_interface: Applied to the face or a local skin area under occlusion
routes.immune_exposure: Moderate — the barrier is intact, but occlusion raises stratum corneum permeability, which lifts both penetration and sensitisation risk

screening.threshold_note: Intact barrier, but occlusion enhances penetration, so immune exposure sits slightly above an unoccluded topical. Standard gate of 0.50.

routes.name: Injectable Filler
routes.contact_interface: Delivered into the dermis or subcutaneous tissue through a needle
routes.immune_exposure: Highest — the barrier is bypassed entirely and the construct enters the tissue; the only one of the five routes that goes into the body

screening.threshold_note: The construct enters the tissue, where the immune system can recognise it directly. Screened against the strictest gate, 0.35.

routes.name: Topical Film
routes.contact_interface: Spread on the skin surface, drying down to or retaining a protein film, with no occlusion
routes.immune_exposure: Low — the barrier is intact and there is no occlusion, so the construct stays largely outside the stratum corneum

screening.threshold_note: Intact barrier with no occlusion, so immune exposure is low. With neither a needle nor occlusion-driven penetration, membrane penetration becomes the main bottleneck. Applied at room temperature, so the thermal stability requirement is the lowest of the five.

routes.name: Hair Care
routes.contact_interface: Coated onto the hair shaft, contacting tissue that is already keratinised and dead
routes.immune_exposure: Lowest — the hair shaft has no blood vessels, lymphatics or immune cells, so the construct never enters the body

screening.threshold_note: The hair shaft is keratinised dead tissue and the construct never reaches the immune system, so the gate is the widest of the five.
extra_gates: No adverse effect on hair feel

routes.emerging_note: The evidence behind this route is still accumulating. On the surface it carries two established companies, but Trautec's E5 evidence comes from its wound-dressing product (Kefuyan, Jiangsu provincial registration no. 20232141168, registered for wound care rather than hair care); hair care appears only as a proposal in the patent. AMSilk's eADF4(C16) reaches only E1, with the dataset stating its evidence is mainly cell-free and ex vivo. No human or regulatory evidence tied to this indication exists.

tools.measures: Probability that the peptide scavenges free radicals. The predictor emits a separate chelating head; the free-radical-scavenging head is what ranks the antioxidant direction.
tools.threshold_note: The predictor's own activity boundary is 0.5 on the FRS head.
Calibrated on the project's own 20.20 M-peptide library rather than taken from the model's default, so the boundary is a project choice written into the predictor's own details.

tools.measures: Predicted haemolytic activity — lysis of red blood cells.
tools.coverage_note: All 496 constructs carry a value here. Across the wider 20.2 M library the predictor only covers a 500,000-peptide sample.

tools.measures: MHC class I presentation score, used as a proxy for T-cell immunogenicity. A higher score means a stronger predicted binder and therefore greater risk.
tools.threshold_note: The gate is per route — 0.35 for wound dressing and injectable filler, 0.50 for mask/patch and topical film, 0.60 for hair care — and is applied from the route's screening profile rather than from a global constant. For reference, the predictor's own Strong Binder boundary sits at about 0.50, so the two tightened routes are stricter than the model's default and the hair-care route is looser.
tools.coverage_note: Only 117 of the 496 constructs carry an MHC-I value, because the predictor covers peptides of 5-15 aa. The remaining rows are reported as not assessed rather than as passing; a separate MHC-II percent rank covers 326 of them.

tools.measures: B-cell epitope propensity — how likely the peptide is to be recognised by antibodies.
tools.coverage_note: All 496 constructs carry a value in the enrichment table.

tools.measures: Exploratory TemStaPro signal: the mean of the model outputs at six temperature thresholds (40, 45, 50, 55, 60 and 65 °C). This is not a measured melting temperature or a calibrated probability for short peptides.
tools.threshold_note: TemStaPro uses separate binary classifiers at temperature thresholds. The stored mean has not been calibrated on short peptides; it does not establish a safe processing temperature, storage condition or shelf life for a fusion protein.

tools.measures: Exploratory solubility signal from a model of recombinant protein expression. A short-peptide score does not establish the aqueous solubility, expression yield or purification behaviour of the assembled fusion protein.
tools.threshold_note: Use for exploratory comparison only. The final sequence and expression context require separate assessment; no expression conditions are determined by this score.

tools.measures: Cell-penetrating propensity. Load-bearing for the topical routes, where membrane penetration — not injection — is the barrier to entry.

An exploratory, pool-relative ranking under an application route's weighting profile. Includes model signals whose short-peptide applicability is unverified; it is not an activity, safety or experimental-success probability.
tools.threshold_note: Computed by this service per route; the weights and the components are returned alongside the value so it can be reproduced from a single response.

evidence_levels.label: E1
evidence_levels.description: Purified protein, physicochemical or cell-free work

evidence_levels.label: E4
evidence_levels.description: Human use or a controlled clinical study

evidence_levels.label: E5
evidence_levels.description: Regulatory review and post-market safety data
